title: Release audit: bounded_run clears CHECK_CHILD before calling cleanup_check, and install.sh deli
summary: Start the checked shell in a dedicated process group/session, record that group for cleanup, call cleanup_check before clearing CHECK_CHILD or any state it reads, signal the group plus a descendant sweep on every exit path, and commit tests that start a background process from the checked shell and assert it is gone on both success and timeout.
requirements: The installer starts the checked login shell so that it leads a process group of its own, distinct from the installer's group.
In the checked login shell, the observed process group identifier equals the shell's own process identifier.
A successful check stops every process in that dedicated group, including background processes the checked login shell started, before the installer reports success.

A check that exceeds its time bound stops every process in that dedicated group, including background processes the checked login shell started, and the installation fails with a message stating the bound that elapsed.

The check's recorded state is released only after the stop attempt on every exit path — success, timeout, internal failure and interruption — and is released exactly once, so an interruption and the normal return cannot signal the same group twice.
No process started by the checked login shell is still running after the installer has exited, on either the success or the timeout path.
The private temporary check directory is removed on every exit path, so a timed-out check leaves no directory carrying the check's private prefix behind.
The script's own description of the check states that the checked shell is placed in a process group of its own and that the group is stopped on every exit path.
The installer never reads its standard input, so it stays safe to pipe into an interpreter.
All existing installer behavior unrelated to cleanup — login-shell and profile detection, the opt-out settings, re-install and uninstall — keeps working unchanged.
acceptance: When the checked login shell starts a background process and then succeeds, the installer exits successfully and that background process is no longer running.

When the checked login shell starts a background process and then hangs past the time bound, the installer exits non-zero, its error output states the elapsed bound, and that background process is no longer running.
In both the successful and the timed-out case, the process group identifier recorded for the checked login shell equals the shell's own process identifier.
After a timed-out check, no directory carrying the check's private prefix remains in the temporary directory.
The regression tests for the successful and the timed-out check cleanup both pass.
The full existing test suite passes.
The script's description of the check no longer states that the checked shell is kept out of its own process group.
plan_goal: Fix install.sh so a new terminal finds forgel-code on PATH

external_dependencies.name: POSIX shell environment
external_dependencies.interface: Execute the installer and its shell functions with the system POSIX shell: `sh install.sh` or `subprocess.run(["sh", "install.sh"], ...)`. Process-group setup and signalling must use POSIX shell facilities such as `set -m` and `kill -- -PGID`. Tests exercise the same shell script.
external_dependencies.evidence: The release audit finding for task 20261123062514 identifies `install.sh` as the installer containing `bounded_run` and `cleanup_check`, and notes its comment about not putting the checked shell in its own process group. `tests/test_install.py` is the existing pytest suite that exercises the installer.

external_dependencies.name: Process observer
external_dependencies.interface: From pytest, call `os.getpgid(pid)` to read the process-group id of the checked shell and compare it with the child PID. From shell, use the POSIX `ps` interface: `ps -o pgid= -p "$pid"`.
external_dependencies.docs: POSIX `ps` specification (`ps -o pgid= -p pid`); Python standard library `os.getpgid`.
external_dependencies.evidence: The audit cites pytest output and a missing `tests/test_check_cleanup.py`; the repository's tests are Python/pytest (`tests/test_install.py`, `tests/test_packaging.py`, etc.), so `os.getpgid` is available in the test runtime. The dependency declaration specifies the equivalent POSIX `ps` observation interface for shell-side checks.
